learning_outcomes.text: Students know and understand essential boundary conditions and methods for the development of components and systems of the Internet of Things. They can reproduce the essential characteristics of different approaches.

Important aspects of the Internet of Things such as software and cloud platforms, sensor technology, and actuators are understood from an application and software development perspective. Boundary conditions such as input/output possibilities, energy (especially for energetically autonomously operating systems) are analyzed and incorporated into the implementation of the problem solution. The potential of incorporating mathematical and computer science knowledge into small and smallest intelligent systems is understood. The treatment of typical integration issues is correctly implemented.

Students who have successfully completed this module understand how to consider all aspects of embedding Internet of Things systems and those in the Industrie 4.0 area, including their distribution, interfaces, and resource-efficient realization.

Students who have successfully completed this module possess knowledge about the essential aspects of developing Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrie 4.0 systems and can apply this in the creation of concepts, architectures, and implementations.

Students who have successfully completed this module can analyze innovative products and new technological possibilities based on IoT and Industrie 4.0. They understand how to implement these in terms of distribution, interfaces, and resource-efficient realization during development.

Students who have successfully completed this module can cooperate with groups from other disciplines and clearly explain their own technical aspects. They can structure, document, and present their work results at various stages of group collaboration.

Students can adequately assess their individual qualification profile regarding the analysis and development of Internet of Things systems and in the Industrie 4.0 area, and can justify their technological and methodological decisions in a differentiated and well-founded manner.

syllabus_topics: Application areas in private and professional sectors
Design forms and resource-efficient development of typical IoT devices
Components and methods for data acquisition and processing in IoT
Decentralized sensor data fusion, data aggregation, and reduction
Development of software for IoT systems
Software architectures for data storage and analysis in IoT
assessment_rules: The portfolio examination is worth 100 points and consists of five practical work samples (APS) and one written project report (PSC). Each of the five APS can contribute a maximum of 10 points, and the PSC can contribute a maximum of 60 points. There is also an ungraded experimental work component.
